[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: in everyday life two people swap objects simultaneously, and in maths 'a = b, b = a' reads as a symmetric relation. Java rule: assignments run one at a time, so the first overwrites a value that must be saved in a temporary first.
[1] misconception (M) -> SwapWithoutTemp: wrong rule: a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = a[i]; exchanges the two values. Right rule: A temporary variable must save a[i] before it is overwritten: t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t;.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> SwapWithoutTemp: Points to LT: save a[i] in t, copy a[j] into a[i], copy t into a[j], in that order. Inconsistent application: the trace performs the second assignment with the old a[i] (as if both happened at once) on some passes. (here mixing in: "a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = a[i]; exchanges the two values")

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: the exchange idiom, three assignments through a temporary variable that trade the values of two array elements.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: T t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; where t has the element type T.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: (1) t receives a[i]; (2) a[i] receives a[j]; (3) a[j] receives t. Each statement uses the state left by the previous one.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: the values at i and j have traded places. With i = 1 and j = 4 in the deck, 3 of Clubs ends in deck[1] and 2 of Diamonds in deck[4].
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: exactly two elements (and t) change; when i == j nothing changes.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The exchange reads and writes elements only through their indices a[i] and a[j], which must both be in bounds.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each of the three steps is an ordinary assignment whose left side is a single variable (here an array element), executed in order.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): Shuffling is a loop of exchanges with random partner positions; using exchanges guarantees the same cards before and after.
[3] relation_to_neighbour (R): Reversal exchanges a[i] with a[N-1-i] for each i in the first half.
[4] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: t is a Sajaniemi temporary. The exchange reorders an array (the array as organizer) without changing its set of values, the building block of shuffling, reversing and sorting.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> SwapWithoutTemp: Conservation: the set of values in the array is unchanged; doing the same exchange again restores the original order; i == j leaves the array unchanged. Changing the order of the three statements breaks it.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: use the exchange whenever two elements must change places (shuffle, reverse, sort, permute). It is not a copy: to duplicate a value, use one assignment.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The old value must be saved before it is overwritten. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = a[i]; (or the three statements reordered), with a[i] != a[j], leaves both elements equal to the old a[j]
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The temporary must have the element type. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: int t = deck[i]; for a String[] deck (incompatible types)
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Both indices must be legal. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: i or j outside 0..a.length-1 (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
